text.en:
Ravi pulled a small weed out of the garden. Some earth came with it.
"Look, Amma! It has thin strings at the bottom, a thin body, and green flat parts!"
Amma smiled. "Every part of a plant has a job. Let's find out what they do."

A plant has parts.
The root grows under the ground. It holds the plant firmly and takes in water from the soil.
The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
The leaves make food for the plant using sunlight.
The flower grows into a fruit. The fruit has seeds, and seeds grow into new plants.
Look at a plant. The part under the ground is the root. It drinks water from the soil.
The stem stands above the ground. It holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
The leaves are the kitchen of the plant. They use sunlight to make food.
The flower becomes a fruit, and the fruit keeps the seeds safe for new plants.

problem.en: Which part of a tomato plant gives us the tomato, and which part took in the water?

text.en: The tomato is the fruit of the plant.
Water is taken in by the roots from the soil.

why.en: Roots grow under the ground and drink water.

text.en: So: the fruit gives the tomato, and the roots took in the water.

why.en: Each part has its own job.

prompt.en: A friend says that leaves only make the plant look pretty. What will you tell your friend?

requiredIdeas.en: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight.
Roots take in water, and the stem carries it up.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking plants get their food only from the soil.

points.en: Root: holds the plant and takes in water.
Stem: holds the plant up and carries water.
Leaf: makes food. Flower: becomes fruit with seeds.
